assertion: The uninsured rate among US adults aged 19 to 64 years rose from 8.9% in 2024 to 11.2% in 2026, a statistically significant increase.
independent_value: Commonwealth Fund news release as quoted by Medical Daily: 8.9% (2024) to 11.2% (2026); Healthcare Dive: 8.9% to about 11%. Survey-based, working-age only.
searched: Commonwealth Fund 2026 Biennial Health Insurance Survey uninsured 11.2% 8.9%

assertion: Overall, 46% of working-age adults were inadequately insured in 2026: 11% were uninsured, 12% had a coverage gap during the year, and 23% were underinsured.
independent_value: Same split reported by Medical Daily and Healthcare Dive.

assertion: The research firm SSRS surveyed a nationally representative sample of 9360 adults aged 19 years and older from May 7 through July 20, 2026; most analyses focused on 7,362 respondents aged 19 to 64 years.
The share of working-age adults who did not get needed care because of cost rose from 46% in 2022 to 50% in 2026, a statistically significant increase that also held among people insured all year.
independent_value: Medical Daily and Healthcare Dive both report 46% to 50%. The 'because of cost' is the survey's own self-reported item definition, not an inferred cause.

assertion: Effectuated marketplace enrollment, which counts only people who paid their premiums, fell 13%, from 22.1 million in 2025 to 19.2 million in February 2026, according to a KFF analysis.
warehouse_value: CMS effectuated enrollment, February: 2025 = 21.78M, 2026 = 19.17M (-12.0%); 2025 full-year average about 22.4M per table notes
sql: SELECT benefit_year, month_num, effectuated_enrollment FROM health.aca_effectuated_enrollment_monthly WHERE geo_level='National' AND platform='All' AND month_num=2 AND benefit_year IN (2024,2025,2026)
independent_value: KFF (June 29, 2026): dropped 13% from a high of 22.1 million in 2025 to 19.2 million in February 2026; ASPE brief says 19.2M.
reason: 22.1M is KFF's 2025 peak; like-for-like February drop is about 12%. Immaterial.

assertion: The administration has attributed the drop to its antifraud efforts.
independent_value: ASPE brief credits program-integrity efforts; KFF notes the same attribution.

assertion: More than half of marketplace enrollees did not get needed care because of cost, and one-third were paying off medical bills over time, compared with 43% and 31%, respectively, among people with employer coverage.
independent_value: Medical Daily: more than half of marketplace enrollees, one-third paying bills; 43% and 31% for job-based coverage. 'Because of cost' is the survey item's own definition.

assertion: Among adults insured all year, 30% were underinsured, including 29% of those with employer-sponsored insurance and half of marketplace enrollees; 19% of marketplace enrollees moved to lower-premium plans.
reason: Commonwealth Fund report returned HTTP 403 and no readable copy carried 30%, 29% or 19%; not an obvious error.
searched: Commonwealth Fund 2026 biennial survey underinsured employer 29% marketplace

assertion: Nearly three-quarters (73%) of adults aged 19 years and older said the federal government has a responsibility to ensure all Americans have health coverage, including 93% of Democrats, 76% of Independents, and 45% of Republicans.
independent_value: Healthcare Dive confirms 73%; the party splits (93/76/45) were not found in any readable copy.
reason: Headline 73% verified; party splits not independently seen.

assertion: The expiration of enhanced tax credits raised average annual premiums by $750 to $4035 depending on income.
reason: Attributed to the report, which returned HTTP 403; no copy carried the range. KFF reports an average 114% payment increase, directionally consistent.
measure: enhanced premium tax credit expiration average premium increase by income
searched: Commonwealth Fund 2026 biennial survey enhanced premium tax credits $750 $4,035

assertion: Changes are projected to produce net Medicaid enrollment losses of 11.5 million over the next decade. The Congressional Budget Office projects separate marketplace changes, combined with rising premiums, will reduce enrollment by 7.5 million.
reason: Could not locate either figure in a source I could open. Healthcare Dive cites an Urban Institute estimate of up to 10 million losing Medicaid, a different estimate.
measure: CBO projected Medicaid enrollment loss H.R. 1 work requirements
searched: H.R. 1 Medicaid enrollment loss 11.5 million CBO marketplace 7.5 million

assertion: Medicaid work requirements of 80 hours per month for most expansion enrollees take effect in 2027.
independent_value: Healthcare Dive and Medical Daily confirm 2027 start and 80 hours.
